glossary.definition: The slide-21 table of the Privilege Capability Overview deck: one row per OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 category, the Privilege component that covers it (Gateway, AIGuard or both), and how, with the two stated gaps (ASI04, ASI06) in amber.
An attacker smuggles instructions into content the agent reads and steers it away from its real goal. Privilege answers with injection, jailbreak and hidden-instruction detection in AIGuard.
Agents acting with over-broad or shared credentials turn a compromise into a privilege compromise. Privilege answers with per-user virtual keys, least-privilege scopes, RBAC and live revocation.
Malicious tool definitions and typosquatted tools install attacker behaviour before a run. AIGuard detects both; fingerprint pinning is the stated remaining gap.
A fact or instruction planted in agent memory changes every future decision. Memory-write inspection ships in AIGuard; gateway integration is in progress.
One runaway agent amplifies through the chain. The gateway caps rate and budget, trips a circuit breaker and streams events to the SIEM; behaviour scoring supplements this and ASI10.
Unregistered agents have no owner, scope or audit trail. No agent reaches a model, tool or peer without a valid scoped key from the agent registry.
Privilege's identity and chokepoint layer: it proves who the agent is and what it may do on every hop.
Privilege's content and behaviour layer: it inspects prompts, tool requests, tool definitions, code-shaped payloads, memory writes and outputs.

stories.title: The coverage table
stories.say: Start with the slide-21 table: all ten ASI categories, who covers each (Gateway, AIGuard or both), and how - with the two stated gaps in amber.

stories.title: ASI01: Agent Goal Hijack
stories.say: An attacker smuggles instructions into content the agent reads and steers it away from its real goal. AIGuard inspects prompts and retrieved content before the agent acts.

stories.title: ASI03: Identity and Privilege Abuse
stories.say: Agents act with credentials; an over-privileged agent turns a compromise into a privilege compromise. Privilege re-binds every call to the human it acts for, narrows scope, and can revoke live.

stories.title: ASI04: Agentic Supply Chain
stories.say: Malicious tool definitions and typosquatted tools install attacker behaviour before a run. AIGuard detects both; fingerprint pinning is the stated remaining gap.

stories.title: ASI06: Memory and Context Poisoning
stories.say: A planted fact in agent memory becomes a standing backdoor across sessions. Memory-write inspection ships in AIGuard; gateway integration is in progress.

stories.title: ASI08: Cascading Agent Failures
stories.say: One runaway agent amplifies through the chain until a small failure is an outage or a bill. The gateway caps rate and budget, trips a circuit breaker, and streams events to your SIEM.

stories.title: ASI10: Rogue Agents
stories.say: Unregistered agents have no owner, scope or audit trail. No agent reaches a model, tool or peer without a valid scoped key.

stories.title: Gateway vs AIGuard
stories.say: The gateway proves who the agent is and what it may do; AIGuard inspects what flows through. ASI03 and ASI07 need both.
